message.content:
Two research tasks for the Nxeon hosting platform (a Hostinger-style VPS + shared-hosting + game-server + email + domains business). Produce concise, ACTIONABLE findings — not essays. Use web search/fetch.

TASK 1 — Ultahost competitive study. Study ultahost.com's shared hosting + VPS products and marketing. Deliver:
- Their product lineup + entry prices (shared hosting, VPS) as of now.
- 5-8 specific things they do well that Nxeon could adopt (features, positioning, guarantees, UX, trust signals) — each as a one-line, concretely-actionable recommendation.
- Anything they claim that Nxeon already does better (so marketing can lean on it).
Keep it to a tight bulleted list with real numbers where visible.

TASK 2 — Hostinger API evaluation. Review the Hostinger developer API at https://developers.hostinger.com/ . Nxeon runs its own Proxmox-based provisioning, billing, DNS (Namecheap), and mail (Mailcow) — it does NOT resell Hostinger. So assess: is there anything in Hostinger's API surface (endpoint design, resource model, webhook/event patterns, DNS/domain/VPS API ergonomics) worth borrowing as a design reference for Nxeon's OWN public/customer API or internal architecture? Deliver 4-6 concrete "worth borrowing" or "not applicable because…" bullets. Be honest if the answer is mostly "not applicable — it's a reseller/consumer API."

OUTPUT: return a single markdown document with two clearly-headed sections (## Ultahost, ## Hostinger API), each a tight actionable bullet list. This is a report to the orchestrator (not shown to a human) — no preamble, just the findings. Do not edit any repo files.

# Hostinger API Structure Overview

## Endpoint Naming Patterns

Hostinger uses a versioned REST API with consistent path conventions. Service endpoints follow the pattern `/api/{service}/v1/`, where services are organized by functional domain (billing, DNS, domains, hosting, etc.).

## Resource Model

The API organizes resources across multiple service categories:

- **Hosting**: Covers datacenters, domains, orders, websites, databases, subdomains, parked domains, NodeJS, and WordPress
- **VPS**: Virtual machines, Docker management, firewalls, public keys, OS templates, backups, snapshots, and malware scanning
- **DNS**: Zone and snapshot management
- **Domains**: Availability checks, forwarding, portfolio, and WHOIS data
- **Billing**: Catalogs, payment methods, and subscriptions
- **Ecommerce**: Store management
- **Reach**: Contact and profile segmentation
- **Horizons**: AI-powered website builder

## Versioning

The API uses explicit version numbering in paths: "v1" appears consistently across all service endpoints, indicating a first major version.

## Authentication

The system implements "Bearer token authentication via `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_TOKEN` header." API tokens are provisioned through the user account at hpanel.hostinger.com/profile/api.

## Integration Tools

Beyond REST endpoints, Hostinger provides SDKs (Python, TypeScript, PHP), a CLI tool, Terraform provider, Ansible collection, MCP server, n8n integration, WHMCS module, and Postman collections—suggesting support for both synchronous and automation-focused patterns.

No explicit webhook/async action documentation appears in this reference material.

## Hostinger API V1 Endpoint Design

The Hostinger API includes several key billing-related endpoints:

- **Catalog**: `GET /api/billing/v1/catalog` - Get catalog item list
- **Orders**: `POST /api/billing/v1/orders` - Create purchase order
- **Payment Methods**: 
  - `GET /api/billing/v1/payment-methods` - Get payment method list
  - `POST /api/billing/v1/payment-methods/{paymentMethodId}` - Set default payment method
  - `DELETE /api/billing/v1/payment-methods/{paymentMethodId}` - Delete payment method
- **Subscriptions**: `DELETE /api/billing/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}/auto-renewal/disable` - Disable auto-renewal

## Key Functionality

The unified order endpoint places an order for one or more catalog items and works across all Hostinger products, leveraging the existing billing infrastructure. Use the catalog endpoint to look up the item_id values available for purchase.

The payment methods and subscriptions system provides programmatic access to: Payment Methods (retrieve available payment methods, set default methods, and remove unused methods) and Subscriptions (monitor active subscriptions, view billing details, and cancel services).

## Ultahost

**Product lineup + entry prices (Aug 2026):**
- **Shared hosting** (cPanel, 2-yr term pricing): Starter $3.44/mo (30GB NVMe, 1 site, ~10k visits) → Basic $5.18/mo (60GB, 4 sites) → Business $10.35/mo (80GB, unlimited sites) → Pro $13.23/mo (110GB). Month-to-month starts ~$3.29; headline "from $2.50/mo" on 3-yr.
- **VPS** (KVM, AMD EPYC, NVMe, "managed"): VPS Basic $4.80/mo (1 vCPU, 1GB RAM, 30GB NVMe, 1 IPv4 + 4 IPv6) → mid ~$13.80/mo → high ~$17.99/mo. All plans: unlimited bandwidth, 99.99% uptime.
- Positioning: deliberately wedged **between budget hosts and managed-premium** — "better performance/security than commodity, cheaper than enterprise" for SMBs.

**Worth adopting (each concretely actionable):**
- **Free hands-off migration as a headline promise** — "our engineers move files, DB, SSL and verify it works, 24/7, no charge." Make this a hero bullet, not fine print; it directly de-risks switching to Nxeon.
- **Bundle security into every tier and name the vendors** — DDoS protection, WAF, malware scanning (they cite Monarx + BitNinja by name). Named third-party security reads as more credible than "secure hosting."
- **Concrete "monthly visits" sizing per plan** (~10k/15k/25k/49k) instead of vague "storage/bandwidth" — helps non-technical buyers self-select a tier. Add this to Nxeon shared-hosting cards.
- **99.99% uptime + 30-day money-back stated on every product page**, side by side. Nxeon should surface both as a fixed trust strip across shared/VPS/game pages.
- **Aggressive term-discount ladder with a live promo code** (40–50% base, stacking to ~80% with codes like "10for10"). A visible countdown/promo mechanic drives conversion; ensure Nxeon shows crossed-out list price vs. discounted price.
- **Star rating + review count as social proof** ("4.9/5 from 1,932 reviews") placed near CTAs. Nxeon should collect and display a real aggregate rating.
- **Free daily backups with multiple restore points** included at every tier — call out "multiple recovery points," not just "backups."
- **NVMe framed with a benefit, not a spec** — "up to 6x faster than standard SSD, pages load near-instantly." Translate Nxeon's NVMe into a speed claim.

**Where Nxeon can claim it does better:**
- Nxeon runs **its own Proxmox provisioning + Mailcow mail + Namecheap DNS stack** — it controls the full stack rather than reselling; lean on "we own the metal/infra, not a middleman."
- Ultahost's "managed VPS" is still shared-panel commodity KVM; Nxeon offers a **true cPanel-style VPS control panel + game servers + integrated email/domains** as one platform (broader product surface than Ultahost's hosting-only catalog).
- Ultahost's low headline prices are **multi-year-term-locked**; Nxeon can differentiate on honest month-to-month pricing / no bait-term if that's the strategy.

## Hostinger API

Reference model: versioned REST, `/api/{service}/v1/...`, Bearer-token auth, services grouped by domain (billing, dns, domains, vps, hosting). Note it is a **first-party consumer/reseller-style API for Hostinger's own panel** — much of the surface (catalog SKUs, Horizons AI builder, Reach) is product-specific and not applicable to Nxeon.

- **Worth borrowing — path convention `/api/{service}/v1/{resource}`.** Clean service-namespaced, explicitly versioned REST. Adopt the same shape for Nxeon's own API (e.g. `/api/vps/v1/machines`, `/api/dns/v1/zones`) so v2 can ship without breaking clients — cheap to copy, pays off long-term.
- **Worth borrowing — unified catalog + order model.** `GET /billing/v1/catalog` returns purchasable `item_id`s; `POST /billing/v1/orders` places one order for one-or-more catalog items and a successful order **generates a subscription**. This decouples "what's for sale" from "buy" and gives one order path across all products — a good fit for Nxeon's mixed VPS/shared/game/domain/mail catalog and existing billing.
- **Worth borrowing — subscription resource with `expires_at` + `is_auto_renewed` and an explicit auto-renewal-disable endpoint** (`DELETE /subscriptions/{id}/auto-renewal/disable`). Clean separation of "cancel service" vs "stop renewing" — worth mirroring in Nxeon's billing so customers can self-serve downgrades.
- **Worth borrowing — PCI boundary drawn at the API.** Payment-method *creation* is deliberately **not** in the API (panel-only, for PCI/security); the API only lists/sets-default/deletes. Nxeon should keep card entry off its own API surface the same way and only expose tokenized payment-method references.
- **Worth borrowing (conceptually) — VPS modeled as a rich resource tree with sub-resources** (firewalls, snapshots, backups, OS templates, PTR records, public keys, malware scanner as nested resources under a VM). Good blueprint for structuring Nxeon's Proxmox-backed VPS API instead of flat RPC endpoints. (Their long-running-action/async-job + webhook patterns weren't documented in what I could reach — so don't assume an event model to copy; Nxeon should design its own job/poll or webhook layer.)
- **Not applicable — the reseller/consumer-specific pieces.** Hostinger's DNS API assumes Hostinger-hosted zones (Nxeon uses Namecheap), its domain/WHOIS/availability endpoints wrap a registrar Nxeon doesn't use, and its mail-DNS status checks (MX/SPF/DKIM/DMARC) overlap what Nxeon already gets from Mailcow's API. Treat these as design references for response *shape* only, not integration targets.
